chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from 'Ula' ibn Razin, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Game is hunted in the state of Ihram (al-Hill), slaughtered in the state of Ihram, brought into the Sanctuary (al-Haram), and eaten.' He said, 'Yes, there is no objection to it.'

And it is not permissible to eat the game slaughtered by the person in Ihram (al-Muhrim) in any state, because it is like the dead meat (al-Maytah). And likewise, if the person released from Ihram (al-Muhill) slaughtered it in the Sanctuary, it was narrated.

key_terms.الْحِلُّ: The state of Ihram (non-sanctuary state during Hajj)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating game hunted or slaughtered during the state of Ihram in Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between the act of hunting and the act of slaughtering during Hajj, establishing that game hunted in the open (al-Hill) remains permissible even if brought into the Sanctuary (al-Haram). It further extends the prohibition of consuming meat slaughtered by the Muhrim (one in Ihram) to include meat slaughtered by the Muḥill (one released from Ihram) within the Sanctuary, treating both as akin to *Maytah* (dead meat) due to the sanctity of the space. This ruling underscores the spatial and ritual purity requirements specific to the Haram, a key topic in Shia fiqh of Hajj.
